---
argmap-version: 0.2
title: "Tutorial: refinement, the core reading move"
description: "One coarse step and the finer argument folded underneath it, and nothing else in the file. Unfolding is what a reader does most in this viewer, and until this file the corpus had no isolated example of it: every map that refines also does five other things at once. The coarse line is a whole judgment stated in one sentence. The block indented under it is the same judgment argued out, and when the map is solved that block REPLACES the coarse line rather than adding to it, so the coarse number stops being an input and becomes a check on the parts."
---

# ===========================================================================
# WHAT REFINEMENT IS: indentation under an evidence line. That is the entire
# syntax. The indented block is a finer-grained version of the same step, and
# the viewer shows it behind a blue plus sign on the coarse line.
#
# WHAT IT IS NOT: a list of the step's premises. Premises go to the right of
# the given bar on the line itself. A refinement is a different, longer way
# of saying the same thing, with its own statements and its own steps.
#
# WHAT THE SOLVE DOES WITH IT (D38): the refinement replaces the coarse line.
# $pattern below exerts no force of its own once $pattern-fine is present, so
# its authored 0.6 is not a solver input. It is displayed instead as a
# SPECTATOR: a dashed arrow from what the author judged to what the parts
# actually deliver. Author the coarse number BEFORE you write the block and
# the comparison is a free audit of your own holistic judgment.
#
# WHY AUTHORS BOTHER: the coarse line is what a reader sees when the block is
# folded, and folded is the default. A map with no coarse lines shows a
# reader a wall of detail; a map whose coarse lines are honest shows them the
# argument, and lets them ask for the detail one step at a time.
# ===========================================================================

@records [The line ran late on most weekday mornings last month] 0.8: a frontier root, so it keeps its authored pin

@delayed [The 8:14 will be late again tomorrow]:  # check: 0.6

$pattern [last month's record carries over to tomorrow] 0.6 @delayed | @records: the coarse step, and a whole judgment in one line: the recent record is a fair guide to tomorrow
  @works [Engineering work on the northern approach runs through next week] 0.7:
  @cause [Last month's lateness was caused by that work] 0.65:
  $pattern-fine [the cause behind the record is still in place] 0.75 @delayed | @records AND @cause AND @works: the same step argued out: a record predicts tomorrow when the thing that produced it has not gone away

# ---- what to look at ------------------------------------------------------
# Solved 2026-08-04 (D36 defaults, solve_map.py):
#   @records 0.796   @works 0.697   @cause 0.648
#   @delayed  check 0.60 -> 0.619
#   $pattern  0.60 ~> 0.650   (spectator: the dashed arrow, not a tension)
#   $pattern-fine  0.75 -> 0.737
#
# Fold and unfold the plus sign on $pattern and nothing about the numbers
# changes: folding is a display state, and the solve has already used the
# fine line either way. That is the property that makes refinement safe to
# read casually.
#
# The coarse judgment and the delivered rate agree closely here, which is the
# boring and desirable case. When they disagree, one of the two is wrong and
# the map is telling you which pair of things to go and look at.
